MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  September 10, 2024
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Kelley at 5:00 p.m., on September 10, 2024, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on September 6, 2024, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P.
Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Vasquez (arrived at 5:05 pm)
  Mayor Kelley

Absent:  Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch (left meeting at 6:00 pm)

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel ~ Anticipated Litigation. Initiation of litigation
  pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Section 54956.9: (2 potential cases)

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Outlined the requirements of AB2449 and questioned the legality of Mayor
Pro Tem Ruesch teleconferencing in for this meeting.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:03 pm Mayor Kelly recessed to Closed Session. Mayor Kelley reconvened the
meeting at 6:03 pm with four Council Members present and Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch absent.
City Council Minutes  1  September 10, 2024
 REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley reported that the Council was presented facts and circumstances on two
potential cases and declined. The City will not be proceeding with any legal action.

INVOCATION: Council Member Goodell

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Vasquez

MAYOR PUBLIC SAFETY UPDATE ON THE ARIPORT FIRE

Received update from Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes and Fire Chief Cheyne
Maule.

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim September 2024 To Be Hunger Action Month

  Presented proclamation to Linda Lewis, Second Harvest Food Bank Ambassador.

P2. Proclaim September 2024 To Be Children’s Emotional Wellness Month

  Presented proclamation to Amy Betonte.

P3. OCTA I-5 Project Update

  Received presentation from Logan Selleck and Niall Barrett from OCTA.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Valentina Naranjo, M.V.: Introduced herself as the President Emeritus of the Community of
Character Committee for Mission Viejo. She introduced the character trait of the month
“Responsibility” and outlined examples of living responsibly.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Questioned the legality of Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch teleconferencing from
Los Angeles International Airport and outlined Government Code 54953 regarding the Brown Act.
She asked the City Attorney to identify the state statute that Mayor Pro Tem Ruesch is performing
his duties under.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Goodell, to approve
the Consent Calendar outlined below.

City Council Minutes  2  September 10, 2024
 On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ruesch

1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of August 27, 2024, as presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated August 16, 2024, in the Amount of $1,197,910.46

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  Golf Check Register Dated August 16, 2024, in the Amount of $325,132.51

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  General Check Register dated August 23, 2024, in the amount of $1,342,184.43

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register dated August 23, 2024, in the amount of $172,396.81

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  City Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2024

  Received and filed.

7.  City Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2023/24

  Received and filed the accompanying City Treasurer's Annual Report for Fiscal Year
  2023/24.

8.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Monthly Report for July 2024

  Received and filed.

9.  Mission Viejo Community Development Financing Authority (MVCDFA) Treasurer’s
  Annual Report for Fiscal Year 2023/24

  Received and filed.

City Council Minutes  3  September 10, 2024
 10. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Monthly Report for July 2024

  Received and filed the accompanying MVCDFA Treasurer's Annual Report for FY 2023/24.

11. Mission Viejo Housing Authority (MVHA) Treasurer’s Annual Report for Fiscal Year
  2023/24.

  Received and filed.

12. Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency Treasurer’s Monthly Report
  for July 2024

  Received and filed accompanying MVHA Treasurer's Report for FY 2023/24.

13. Biennial Update of the City of Mission Viejo’s Conflict of Interest Code

  Adopted Resolution 24-43 Amending the City of Mission Viejo's Conflict of Interest Code.

14. FY 2024/25 Investment Policies

  (1) Adopted Resolution 24-44 Approving the City's Investment Policy for FY 2024/25; (2)
  adopted Housing Authority Resolution 24-03 Approving the Investment Policy for 2024/25;
  and (3) adopted Community Development Financing Resolution 24-02 Approving the
  CDFA Investment Policy for FY 2024/25.

15. 2023 Residential Resurfacing-Asphalt Repairs and Asphalt Overlays (CIP 24838)-
  Notice of Completion

  (1) Certified the completion of and accept the improvements for the subject project; (2)
  authorize the City Manager to sign the Notice of Completion; (3) authorize the City Clerk to
  record the Notice of Completion with the County of Orange and to release the faithful
  performance and payment bonds one year and 35 days, respectively, after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion contingent upon no claims or liens being filed with
  the City; and (4) authorize the release of the final retention 35 days after the date of
  recordation of the Notice of Completion.

16. Residential Resurfacing-Slurry Seal (CIP 25838)-Award of Contract

  Awarded the construction contract for the subject project to Roy Allan Slurry Seal, Inc.,
  (A24-30) in the amount of $982,690.75.

OLD BUSINESS

17. LOS OSOS Phase I - (CIP 336)

Assistant City Manager Jerry Hill presented the staff report.
City Council Minutes  4  September 10, 2024
 Pam Smith, M.V., and Robert Breton M.V.: Spoke in favor of the project and indicated that the
many residents they have spoken with are very excited to see this project start.

Cathy Schlicht, M.V.: Stated that the Vision Plan violates the CC&R’s, and that the public should
be aware of the pending lawsuit against these violations with a jury trial date in August 2025. She
stressed that all spending should be pause until the outcome of that trial. Accused the Council of
putting tax dollars at risk and outlined the spending thus far.

Council Member Vasquez asked what the status was for the environmental assessments.

Assistant City Manager Hill stated that Carlson Strategic filed the notice of exemption for the
phase one area and the urban alley, which is everything up to the creek.

Council Member Bucknum asked where the Farmers Market and Night Market will be located
during construction.

Assistant City Manager Hill stated that they will be temporarily moved to the City Hall parking
lot.

Motion made by Council Member Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Kelley, to (1) approve the Plans
and Specifications and authorize staff to advertise bids for Los Osos Phase I-(CIP 336); (2) award
a contract for the purchase and installation of a Prefabricated Restroom Building to Public
Restroom Company (A24-32) in an amount not to exceed $299,510.00; (3) award a contract for
the purchase and installation of the Office/Concession Building to Public Restroom Company
(A24-33) in amount not to exceed $805,114.00; (4) approve issuance of Purchase Order for the
purchase of Security Lighting Poles to Ameron Pole Products in the amount not to exceed
$70,844.00; (5) approve issuance of Purchase Order for purchase of Security Lighting Fixtures
and Arms to Linx Lighting and Controls in an amount not to exceed $84,409.10; and (6) approve
issuance of Purchase Order for the Main Electrical Switch Gear to CED in an amount not to exceed
$67,002.03.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  Ruesch

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

18. Orange County Local Agency Formation Commission (LAFCO) Report

  Receive written report.

City Council Minutes  5  September 10, 2024
 COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

19. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

  By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars
  as presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public
  record.

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum apologized for not attending the last meeting. She was visiting family
in Hawaii. She stated she had a great summer and mentioned that she had a wonderful time
attending the Prelude in the Park and National Night Out with her grandchildren. Council Member
Bucknum complimented City Manager Lister on doing a great job this summer. She also pointed
out to the residents about the illegal street carts and reminded residents that the Health Department
has not certified them. She encouraged residents to please go to the businesses instead of
purchasing from these carts which are organized from Los Angeles. The only way to stop them
from continuing to come and set up in Mission Viejo is to not purchase from them. Lastly, she
invited residents to attend the Patriot Day Ceremony tomorrow at 5:30 pm at the Potocki Trailhead
just below the soccer fields.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell reported that he attended the 30th Anniversary for the Animal Services
Center and that it was a wonderful event. He also attended a luncheon with the Korean Consul
General Wan-Joong Kim in Los Angeles along with Representative Young Kim to discuss our
economic and sports tourism programs in our city. Lastly, he stated he is looking forward to the
Patriots Day event tomorrow.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez stated she was not in attendance at the last meeting due to an illness.
Indicated she has a great summer with the family attending many events including the Wild Rivers
ACCOC Annual Roundtable and Reception. She also attended the Symphony in the Park and
National Night Out. Council Member Vasquez expressed that we need more face painters at events
as that seems to be very popular. Lastly, she mentioned that she donated her hair to an organization
called Children with Hair Loss, so if you are interested the website is
www.childrenwithhairloss.org.

Mayor Kelley

Mayor Kelley addressed Council Member Vasquez that the Community of Character Committee
will be having more face painting at events. She encouraged residents to continue receive updates
on the fire and to keep the firefighters, police, emergency responders, and animal services in your
prayers. Mayor Kelley reported that she received a phone call last evening from Congresswoman
City Council Minutes  6  September 10, 2024
 Young Kim asking how Mission Viejo is holding up with the fire. She encouraged residents to
attend the Patriot Day Ceremony tomorrow as well as Restaurant Week which is put on by the
Chamber of Commerce. She mentioned that she was attending an event earlier today with the
CEO of the Chamber of Commerce and he commented that restaurants in Mission Viejo are
struggling, so she encouraged residents to patron our restaurants. Residents can find information
on Restaurant week on the chamber of Commerce website. Mayor Kelley also attended the 30th
Anniversary celebration at the Animal Services Center, where items were collected for a time
capsule that will be opened in 30 years. On Sunday she attended the Annual Grandparents Day
Ceremony at Heritage Point Retirement Home. She also attended a Ribbon Cutting Ceremony for
Jovive Wound Care which is a state-of-the-art facility in Mission Viejo. Mayor Kelley attended a
dedication ceremony at the Bocce Ball Courts where Anna T. Boyce and Nino Fiorentino were
named for two of the courts and two benches. Lastly, she attended the Moulton Niguel Water
District’s Public Safety Appreciation Lunch.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:37 p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Kelley adjourned the meeting in memory of Senior Corps of Retirees Member Bob Perry
to Tuesday, September 24, 2024, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of September 24, 2024

City Council Minutes  7  September 10, 2024
